body: # 1800 GOT JUNK Boston Massachusetts Prices When you type “1800 GOT JUNK Boston Massachusetts Prices” into Google, you’re probably juggling a looming clean‑out, a tight budget, and a desire to avoid surprise charges. This guide breaks down exactly how 1‑800‑GOT‑JUNK calculates its rates in the Boston area, shows you real‑world pricing scenarios, compares the company to local competitors, and equips you with insider tips to keep the final bill predictable. By the end you’ll know which service gives the most **bang for your buck**, and how to prepare your junk so the crew can work at peak efficiency. --- ## How 1‑800‑GOT‑JUNK Determines Its Prices in Boston Understanding the pricing formula helps you spot where you can save. 1‑800‑GOT‑JUNK uses a **transparent, volume‑based model** rather than a weight‑based system. Below are the key drivers. ### Volume‑Based Pricing * **Cubic yard measurement** – The crew loads your items into their 12‑foot trucks, then measures the occupied space in cubic yards (CY). * **Standard rates** – In 2024 Boston rates range from **$159 for the first 2 CY** up to **$279 for 5 CY**. Anything beyond 5 CY moves into a “custom quote” tier, usually $45‑$55 per additional CY. * **Same‑day service surcharge** – If you need a crew within 24 hours, expect a **$30‑$50 premium** because the dispatcher must prioritize your slot. ### Types of Junk and Special Items | Item Category | Typical Impact on Price | Example | |---------------|------------------------|---------| | **General household junk** | Covered by base volume price | Old couches, broken appliances | | **Large furniture** (e.g., king‑size bed) | May require two‑truck loading, adds **$40‑$70** | Heavy wood frame | | **Electronics** (TV, computer) | No extra fee if non‑hazardous | 55‑inch TV | | **Hazardous waste** (paints, batteries) | Separate disposal, **$50‑$150** per load | Oil‑based paint cans | ### Seasonal and Location Adjustments Boston’s **traffic congestion** and **snow removal** can affect crew travel time. During winter months (December‑February), the company adds a **$15‑$25 “weather adjustment”** for each crew dispatched in the Greater Boston area. Conversely, the off‑peak summer period (July‑August) sometimes sees a **$10 discount** on the base rate for non‑rush jobs. ### What’s Included in the Quote A standard quote **includes:** * Labour (two‑person crew) * Loading and transportation * Full disposal at a licensed landfill or recycling center * Cleanup of the worksite No hidden “dump fees” appear on the invoice—everything is bundled into the per‑cubic‑yard price. --- ## Real‑World Pricing Examples for Common Boston Jobs Numbers speak louder than theory. Below are three typical scenarios, complete with location‑specific adjustments. ### Small Apartment Clean‑Out (1‑Bedroom, Cambridge) * **Volume**: 2 CY (old mattress, sofa, coffee table, boxes) * **Base price**: $159 * **Winter surcharge** (January): +$20 * **Total**: **$179** If the tenant adds a bulky dining set, the crew may need a **second truck** for an extra **$45**. The final bill would be **$224**. ### Whole‑House Declutter (4‑Bedroom, Dorchester) * **Volume**: 5 CY (multiple furniture pieces, appliances, yard waste) * **Base price**: $279 * **Same‑day request**: +$40 * **Hazardous paint cans (2)**: +$80 * **Total**: **$399** The homeowner saved $60 by **pre‑sorting** recyclable metal and sending it to a local scrap yard before the crew arrived. ### Commercial Office Junk Removal (Mid‑size office, Back Bay) * **Volume**: 4 CY (old desks, CRT monitors, carpet rolls) * **Base price**: $239 * **Weekend service** (Saturday): +$30 * **Electronic waste recycling fee** (mandatory for CRTs): +$100 * **Total**: **$369** Because the office opted for **self‑packaging**, the crew loaded items faster, keeping labour time under the standard 2‑hour window and avoiding any overtime charge. > **Tip:** Request a **pre‑visit estimate**. The dispatcher often sends a photo‑request of the junk; a quick snap can lock in the quoted volume before the crew arrives, preventing surprise upgrades. Let’s pit the national chain against three typical local players: **Boston Junk Guys**, **EcoJunk Boston**, and **Metro Haul**. ### Pricing Structure of Local Haulers | Company | Base Rate (first 2 CY) | Additional CY | Same‑Day Surcharge | Hazardous Waste Fee | |---------|------------------------|---------------|--------------------|----------------------| | **1‑800‑GOT‑JUNK** | $159 | $45‑$55 per CY | $30‑$50 | $50‑$150 | | **Boston Junk Guys** | $149 | $40 per CY | $25 | $75 | | **EcoJunk Boston** (recycling focus) | $169 | $50 per CY | $35 | $0 (they handle most recyclables in‑house) | | **Metro Haul** | $139 | $45 per CY | $40 | $100 | ### Service Differences * **Truck fleet** – 1‑800‑GOT‑JUNK operates a **standardized 12‑ft truck fleet**, ensuring consistent capacity. Boston Junk Guys uses mixed‑size trucks, which can mean a smaller vehicle for a large load, potentially requiring a second trip. * **Disposal methods** – EcoJunk Boston emphasizes **recycling**; they separate metals, wood, and plastics on‑site, which can reduce landfill
